findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the database a public endpoint resolvable and reachable from outside the VPC. Combined with a MySQL master user named 'admin', this greatly expands attack surface for credential brute force and exploitation.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, snapshots and read replicas, leaving stored data unencrypted on the underlying storage.
The master username is the default/predictable 'admin', which combined with a publicly accessible endpoint removes one unknown from an online credential-guessing attack.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database will accept unencrypted client connections; the application's mysqli_connect call does not request TLS either.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached through the instance profile to an internet-facing web server, so compromise of the instance (e.g. SSRF to IMDS) yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 and RDS in the account, including data exfiltration and destruction.

user_data interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into a PHP include file. EC2 user data is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and is also stored in the Terraform state, leaking database credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. An SSRF or file-read flaw in the PHP application could be used to steal the instance role credentials, which carry wildcard s3/ec2/rds permissions.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the root volume - which stores the credential-bearing /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc file - is unencrypted at rest unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be enabled.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd with no TLS configuration and serves a form that accepts and displays user data, so all traffic including form submissions traverses the network in cleartext.
Egress from the RDS security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control from anything attached to this group.
